Definition: good for nothing, by anal. vain or vanity; specifically an idol
BiblicalUsage: ʼĕlîyl is a plain word for an idol, a worthless thing. In Leviticus 19:4, the text says "Turn ye not unto idols." In 1 Chronicles 16:26, the text says "For all the gods of the people [are] idols."
TheologicalSignificance: ʼĕlîyl convinces me that idols promise what only God can give, and they always leave their worshippers empty. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
